text:
maria: spun up a quick bring-up for nova-embed-int6 on the staging stack. ran the standard holdout recall and a small cluster sanity. dropping the run summary here.

maria: command run:
```bash
./eval_embeddings --model nova-embed-int6 --holdout holdout_v3 --metrics recall@1,recall@5,precision@5 --calib 20k
```

ci-bot: eval job 5901 completed — recall@1: 0.398, recall@5: 0.736, precision@5: 0.582
ci-bot: compare baseline (nova-int8) — recall@1: 0.435, recall@5: 0.798, precision@5: 0.614

sam: roughly 6.2% abs drop at R@5 again. any obvious strat differences?

maria: quick slice shows short queries (<6 tokens) worst affected. also seeing compressed score distributions (smaller cosine gaps).

raj: what quant flow? per-tensor or per-channel? symmetric vs asym?

maria: default int6 pipeline: per-tensor symmetric with global clamp. used a random calib 20k.

raj: per-tensor symmetric can crush layerwise activations. try per-channel asymmetric + per-layer clamp tuning. also test an L2-normalize-in-quant pipeline to preserve cosine angles.

olivia: can we also check cluster purity via silhouette for the top classes? might reveal spurious neighbors.

maria: running silhouette + topk-idflip dump now. dumping artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/nova-int6/5901/

ci-bot: job 5902 queued (per-channel-asym, calib=100k, silhouette + idflip)

sam: also recommend a mini in-prod record-only canary: route 5% traffic to int6 and capture embeddings, serve int8. gives us real distribution.

olivia: +1, add console flag record-only and create a deployment tag.

raj: beware of kv-cache effects. if vector norms shift we might see retrieval delta due to precomputed key normalization.

maria: noted. adding norm-preserve postproc to eval and will compare norm histograms.

ci-bot: job 5902 finished — new metrics: recall@5: 0.764 (improved), R@1: 0.412, silhouette delta -0.03 vs int8, top1 idflip rate (short queries) 14%.

maria: per-channel-asym + larger calib helped but still not parity. histogram shows int6 vectors have slightly lower L2 norms on avg.

sam: try a per-axis rescale to match int8 norm distribution — cheap to do offline and re-eval. also test hybrid router rule: if query_len>10 -> int6 embedding else int8.

olivia: would like cohort breakdown (support articles, search, chat) — which domain loses the most.

maria: cohort quickslice: support R@5 -0.09, search -0.04, chat -0.02. support queries are short and templated.

raj: suggests calibration set underrepresents templated support queries. create a stratified calib with heavier support sampling and rerun.

maria: launching stratified calib 150k with support weight 0.5.

ci-bot: job 5903 queued (stratified calib 150k)

maria: also capturing neighbor diffs (id + score) for 10k random queries to inspect semantic degradations.

ci-bot: job 5903 finished partial — support cohort R@5 moved from 0.69 -> 0.74, overall R@5 0.782. idflip short-query now 9%.

sam: good progress. two questions: 1) after per-axis rescale does R@5 hit within 1% abs of int8? 2) what's the tail behavior (worst 1% queries)?

maria: will run per-axis rescale and a tail analysis (worst decile + worst 1%).

olivia: please open a ticket linking the eval jobs and s3 artifacts. I'll hold the console rollout until we meet the gate: delta R@5 <= 1% abs and top1 idflip short-queries <7%.

maria: creating ticket ML-1189 with jobs [5901,5902,5903] and s3 path. also scheduling the 5% record-only canary after per-axis rescale run.

ci-bot: created ticket ML-1189 assigned to maria

raj: one more thought — consider training-time (post-hoc) L2 temperature scaling so quantized outputs better preserve relative angles. not for immediate canary but for roadmap.

sam: agree on roadmap idea. for now let's get the stratified calib + per-axis rescale results, then run the paired-significance test on canary samples.

maria: thanks team — will post results when per-axis rescale job completes. linking notebook: https://redwood-internal/notebooks/nova-int6-eval

olivia: thanks! :rocket:

sam: great triage everyone :thumbsup:
